summary: Hojun Nagasaki worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, served as president of the Japan Association of Jain Studies in 1998, and became professor emeritus at Otani University by 1999.
Hokai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hogetsu and Zuihe.
Hokei Izumi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and under Bunyiu Nanjio, later serving as a professor at Otani University (attested 1930).
Hoko Kuwana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (attested 2015) and held a post at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2001-2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2008.

Holmes Welch was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his B.A. and M.A. at Harvard University (~1940-1957) and served as a lecturer at both Harvard and Yale University.

Hong Luo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After earning a PhD at Peking University in 2007, he served at China Tibetology Research Center (2007-2017), Sichuan University (2018), and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Hongyue Guo specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Guo studied under Xubang Qi and completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007) under the supervision of Stephen R. Bokenkamp.

Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1963 and 1992), Minobusan University (attested 1996), and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (attested 1996).
Hoong Teik Toh is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Toh earned a PhD from Harvard University by 2004, studying under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales was an archaeologist and Indologist. Educated at Cambridge and SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden, he held positions at King's College Bangkok, the Greater India Society (~1934-1941), and the Royal Asiatic Society (1964-1968).

Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital. He served as Boden Professor of Sanscrit at the University of Oxford (1831-1860) and held posts at the East India Company and Royal Asiatic Society.

Horace L. Friess worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University and Heidelberg University, later serving on Columbia University's faculty from 1919 and as Joseph L. Buttenwieser Professor (1962-1966), alongside a post at Johns Hopkins.
Horkhang Sonam Palbar was a scholar in Tibetology who studied under Tsadru Ngawang Losang and Gendun Chophel (~1946-1951).
Horst Brinkhaus is an Indologist who held academic positions at the University of Münster (attested 1978) and Kiel University (~1995-2008).

Horst Lasic is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999, served as a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995), and lectured at Vienna in 1999.

Hosakote Krishna Sastri was an archaeologist and Indologist. He worked at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1892-1925), serving as Government Epigraphist (~1920-1925), and also lectured at the University of Calcutta.
Hoseok Leigh works in philosophy and religious studies. Leigh studied under Ha-u Kim and Cheonghwa, completing a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).
Hoseong Kim works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2011, Kim served as a professor at Dongguk University and founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo.
Hoshu Mitsuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1982) and later professor emeritus (attested 2004) at Koyasan University.
